questions.q: The cationic carbon of a simple alkyl carbocation such as (CH₃)₃C⁺ is
options: sp³ hybridised, pyramidal, with a lone pair
sp² hybridised, trigonal planar, with an empty p orbital
sp² hybridised, trigonal planar, with a filled p orbital
questions.explain: A carbocation carbon has only six valence electrons; it is sp² and planar, and the empty p orbital makes it an electrophile and Lewis acid.

questions.q: 3-Methylbut-1-ene reacts with HCl. The product formed by carbocation rearrangement is
questions.explain: Protonation gives a 2° cation next to a C–H on a tertiary carbon; a 1,2-hydride shift makes the more stable 3° cation, which Cl⁻ captures to give 2-chloro-2-methylbutane. 2-Chloro-3-methylbutane is the unrearranged product.

questions.q: Which aryl group has the highest migratory aptitude in a 1,2-shift to a carbocation?
questions.explain: Electron-donating para groups help the migrating ring carry the positive charge, so the order is p-anisyl > p-tolyl > phenyl > p-nitrophenyl.

questions.q: The 1-cyclopentylethyl cation rearranges. The final, most stable cation formed is
questions.explain: Ring expansion first gives the 2° 2-methylcyclohexyl cation (less strain), and a 1,2-hydride shift then gives the 3° 1-methylcyclohexyl cation. Stopping at the 2-methylcyclohexyl cation is the trap.
